senses.en: a large heavy animal of the cow family, used in Asia for pulling ploughs and carts
examples: A **buffalo** was standing in the middle of the paddy field.
My grandfather still uses a **buffalo** to plough the rice fields.
The boys rode the **buffalo** home along the river path.

buffalo.note: In Viet Nam this almost always means the **water buffalo**. The plural can be *buffalo* (unchanged) or *buffaloes* — both are correct.

senses.en: a field filled with shallow water where rice is grown
senses.vi: ruộng lúa nước, cánh đồng lúa
examples: The **paddy fields** turn bright green in early summer.
We walked along the narrow path between two **paddy fields**.
Her parents work in the **paddy fields** from dawn.

paddy field.note: Also written *rice paddy* or just *paddy*. *Paddy* on its own can also mean rice that still has its husk on.

senses.en: the time when crops are gathered from the fields, or the crops that are gathered
examples: The rice **harvest** begins in October.
It was a good **harvest** this year — the best for a decade.
The whole village helps at **harvest** time.

senses.en: to gather a crop from the fields
examples: They **harvest** the rice twice a year.
The corn is **harvested** in late August.

senses.en: a piece of land where fruit trees are grown
examples: My uncle has an **orchard** behind his house.
We picked apples in the **orchard** all morning.
The **orchard** is full of mango trees.

orchard.note: An **orchard** is for fruit *trees*. A *garden* is a general word, and a *vegetable garden* grows vegetables instead.

senses.en: cows and bulls kept on a farm for their milk or meat
examples: The **cattle** are grazing in the field.
His family keeps about forty **cattle**.
We drove the **cattle** down to the stream to drink.

cattle.note: **Always plural** — *the cattle **are** in the field*, never *is*. There is no form *a cattle* or *cattles*; for one animal say *a cow* or *a bull*.

senses.en: a large group of animals of the same kind that live or are kept together
examples: A **herd** of buffalo crossed the road in front of us.
The farmer has a **herd** of thirty cows.
We watched a **herd** of elephants at the waterhole.

senses.en: to move animals, or people, together as a group
examples: The boy **herded** the goats back to the barn.
We were **herded** onto the bus like sheep.

herd.note: Use **herd** for cows, buffalo and elephants; *flock* for birds and sheep; *school* for fish. Sounds exactly like *heard*.

senses.en: a large farm building used for storing crops or keeping animals in
senses.vi: nhà kho, chuồng gia súc (ở trang trại)
examples: The hay is kept in the **barn**.
We shelter the cattle in the **barn** in winter.
There is an old wooden **barn** behind the farmhouse.

senses.en: a deep hole dug in the ground to reach water
examples: Every morning she draws water from the **well**.
The village **well** dried up during the drought.
There is an old stone **well** in the yard.

senses.en: in a good or satisfactory way
examples: She sings very **well**.
He didn't sleep **well** last night.

well.note: In this unit it is the **noun** — a hole for water. Do not confuse the adverb *well* (*she plays well*) with the adjective *good* (*she is a good player*).

senses.en: a small narrow river
examples: The children were playing in the **stream**.
A small **stream** runs behind our house.
We crossed the **stream** on stepping stones.

senses.en: to send or receive video or music over the internet as it plays
examples: We **streamed** the match on my phone.
The concert was **streamed** live.

stream.note: Size order: a **stream** is smaller than a *river*; a *brook* is smaller still.

senses.en: a tall tropical plant with hard hollow stems, used for building and for making furniture
examples: The fence is made of **bamboo**.
**Bamboo** grows very quickly — up to a metre a day.
She was carrying two baskets on a **bamboo** pole.

bamboo.note: Usually uncountable when you mean the material: *made of bamboo*. Stress the second syllable: bam-**BOO**.

senses.en: extremely large in area or amount
examples: A **vast** paddy field stretched to the mountains.
The country has **vast** areas of forest.
There is a **vast** difference between the two villages.

forms.en: very much; to a great degree
forms.ex: Life here is **vastly** different from the city.

vast.note: Stronger than *big* or *large*, and used for open space or quantity — not usually for a single object. Rhymes with *fast*.

senses.en: quiet and calm, without noise or worry
examples: The countryside is much more **peaceful** than the city.
We spent a **peaceful** afternoon by the stream.
It is so **peaceful** here in the early morning.

senses.en: not involving war, violence or argument
examples: They found a **peaceful** solution to the dispute.
It was a **peaceful** protest.

forms.en: a situation with no war, or a state of calm
forms.ex: I just want a bit of **peace** and quiet.

senses.en: to put a large quantity of things onto a vehicle or into a container
examples: They **loaded** the rice onto the cart.
Help me **load** the truck before it rains.
The buffalo cart was **loaded** with bamboo.

senses.en: something heavy that is being carried
examples: He carried a heavy **load** of firewood.
That's the third **load** of hay today.

load.note: Opposite: **unload**. Note the pair *load the cart* (the cart is the object) and *load the rice onto the cart* (the rice is).

senses.en: to take fruit off a tree or plant by hand
examples: In summer we **pick fruit** in my uncle's orchard.
The children love to **pick fruit** straight from the tree.
We spent the morning **picking fruit** and the afternoon swimming.

pick fruit.note: **Pick** here means take *off* the plant. *Pick up* is different — it means lift something from the ground.

senses.en: to gather eggs from where hens have laid them
examples: Every morning I **collect eggs** from the hen house.
It's my job to **collect the eggs** before school.
She **collected** six **eggs** today.
colloc: collect eggs from the hen house

senses.en: to sit on a horse and control it as it moves
examples: My cousin can **ride a horse** very well.
I learned to **ride a horse** when I was eight.
They **rode horses** along the beach at sunset.

ride a horse.note: Irregular: ride → **rode** → **ridden**. Use *ride* for horses, bikes and motorbikes; use *drive* for cars.

senses.en: to make a kite rise and stay in the air on the end of a string
examples: On windy afternoons we **fly kites** on the hill.
He taught his little sister to **fly a kite**.
It's too still today — you can't **fly a kite** without wind.
colloc: fly a kite in the wind

senses.en: a member of a group of people who move from place to place instead of living in one
examples: The **nomads** move their herds to new grass each season.
For centuries **nomads** have crossed these plains.
His grandparents were **nomads** before they settled in the village.

forms.en: moving from place to place rather than living in one
forms.vi: du mục, nay đây mai đó
